subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is meant by one-off production?
options: The manufacture of a single, individual product made to a specific requirement
The continuous production of thousands of identical items
Producing a set quantity of identical items in one run
The use of robots to assemble products automatically
questions.explain: One-off (or job/bespoke) production makes a single unique product to meet a particular client's need.

questions.q: Which statement best describes batch production?
options: Producing a specific quantity of identical products in one run
Making one unique item for a single customer
Producing goods continuously 24 hours a day
questions.explain: Batch production makes a set number of identical items, after which equipment can be reset for a different batch.

questions.q: Mass production is best defined as:
options: The large-scale, continuous production of large numbers of identical products
Making a single prototype for testing
Producing small numbers of a product then changing over
Hand-making items to a customer's exact specification
questions.explain: Mass production produces very large quantities of identical products continuously, often on a production line.

questions.q: A tailor makes a single suit measured exactly to one client. Which scale of production is this?
questions.explain: A single item made to one customer's measurements is one-off (bespoke) production.

questions.q: A bakery makes 300 identical loaves, then resets its equipment to make 300 bread rolls. Which scale of production is being used?
questions.explain: Making a set quantity then changing over to a different product is characteristic of batch production.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of mass production compared with one-off production?
options: A lower cost per unit (unit cost)
Greater flexibility to change the design frequently
Higher skill required from each worker per item
Products that are all uniquely different
questions.explain: Large volumes and economies of scale spread costs, giving mass production a low unit cost.

questions.q: Why does one-off production usually cost more per item than mass production?
options: It relies heavily on skilled labour and cannot share set-up costs over many items
It always uses more expensive raw materials
It is fully automated with costly robots
It uses cheaper tooling than mass production
questions.explain: Bespoke items need skilled labour and time, and their costs cannot be spread across a large volume.

questions.q: Injection moulding is mainly used to shape which type of material?
questions.explain: Injection moulding forces molten thermoplastic into a mould to form complex 3D shapes.

questions.q: Which industrial process is used to make hollow plastic items such as drinks bottles?
questions.explain: Blow moulding inflates a heated plastic tube against a mould to create hollow items like bottles.

questions.q: In vacuum forming, how is the plastic shaped over the mould?
options: A heated thermoplastic sheet is sucked over a mould by removing the air beneath it
Molten plastic is injected under high pressure
Molten metal is poured into a cavity
Plastic granules are compressed and heated in a screw
questions.explain: Vacuum forming heats a thermoplastic sheet then uses suction to pull it tightly over a mould.

questions.q: Die casting is a process used to shape:
questions.explain: Die casting forces molten metal into a reusable metal mould (die) to make accurate metal components.

questions.q: A company needs to make millions of identical rigid plastic bottle caps quickly and accurately. Which process is most suitable?
questions.explain: Injection moulding is ideal for high-volume production of small, detailed, identical plastic parts.

questions.q: A firm wants long aluminium lengths with the same cross-section for window frames. Which process suits this best?
questions.explain: Extrusion pushes material through a shaped die to produce a continuous length with a constant cross-section.

questions.q: What does CAD stand for?
questions.explain: CAD is Computer Aided Design, using software to create and modify designs on screen.

questions.q: What does CAM stand for?
questions.explain: CAM is Computer Aided Manufacture, using computer-controlled machinery to make products.

questions.q: A CNC machine is described as computer numerical control. What does this mean?
options: The machine is controlled by numerical data (a program) from a computer
The machine is operated entirely by hand with no electricity
The machine can only cut wood
The machine designs products without any input
questions.explain: CNC machines follow coded numerical instructions from a computer to control their movements precisely.

questions.q: Which is a key benefit of using CAD/CAM in manufacturing?
options: Consistent accuracy and repeatability of identical products
Every product is guaranteed to be uniquely different
It removes the need for any quality checks
It always makes small one-off items cheaper than mass items
questions.explain: CAD/CAM links design directly to machining, producing highly accurate, repeatable, identical parts.

questions.q: What is meant by quality control (QC)?
options: Checking and testing products against a set standard to identify faults
Advertising a product to increase sales
Designing the packaging for a product
Choosing which colours a product will be made in
questions.explain: Quality control involves inspecting and testing finished or in-progress items against agreed standards.

questions.q: How does quality assurance (QA) differ from quality control (QC)?
options: QA is a system of procedures set up to prevent faults, while QC checks products for faults
QA only tests finished products, while QC designs the product
QA and QC mean exactly the same thing
QA is done by customers, while QC is done by machines only
questions.explain: QA builds quality into the process to prevent defects, whereas QC inspects to detect defects.

questions.q: A component is specified as 50 mm with a tolerance of plus or minus 1 mm. Which measured size is acceptable?
questions.explain: A tolerance of 50 mm plus or minus 1 mm allows any size from 49 mm to 51 mm, so 50.6 mm passes.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Commercial Manufacturing Methods
